hypothesis: does the hub send anything spontaneously on connect
verdict: honest negative, expected: zero spontaneous bytes at any tested rate. Hub almost certainly needs an explicit connect command before streaming.

mode: pull full pneuron.lua source via curl (verbatim, not summarized)
hypothesis: does the public dissector contain the CRC-8 algorithm, not just the framing
verdict: key finding: the file does NOT contain the CRC-8 algorithm, only where the checksum byte sits in the frame. Any command we build will be silently dropped by the hub (bad checksum) without the real algorithm. Also pulled the full skeleton node table and connect/disconnect byte candidates from the author's comments (unconfirmed against the full parser).

mode: pivot: reuse ../reverb-g2's Windows capture kit instead of blind CRC brute-force
hypothesis: reverb-g2 already solved the same generic problem (proprietary protocol, one Windows-side handshake capture needed once) with a reusable kit - adapt it 1:1 for Perception Neuron
verdict: adapted: windows-kit/capture.ps1 (auto-discovers every USBPcap interface, captures all at once), windows-kit RUNBOOK, scripts/parse-pn-capture.py (reuses reverb-g2's dependency-free usb_packets() pcapng reader verbatim, decodes 0xfd...0xfe frames against pneuron.lua's tables). Better than CRC brute-force: replay the real captured bytes, no need to understand the CRC-8 algorithm at all.

mode: active probe from Linux, no reference capture yet: 36 combinations (3 candidate commands x 6 CRC-8 algorithms x 2 dst values) + DTR/RTS toggle, all at 115200 baud
hypothesis: can the connect handshake be found blind before escalating to a Windows capture session
verdict: honest negative, documented before escalating: 0 responses across all 36 combinations, 0 bytes after DTR/RTS toggle. Exhausted what's reasonable to try blind - too many remaining unknowns (id/src values, undocumented framing fields, send baud rate, uncovered CRC algorithms) for brute force without a real reference. The Windows capture session is the real unblock.

mode: first real Windows capture attempt (2 files, run by hand with Wireshark/dumpcap, not capture.ps1, connecting/disconnecting on two different physical USB ports) + Axis Studio license check
hypothesis: does either capture contain the hub's handshake, and can Axis Studio connect to the hub at all
verdict: double negative, both diagnosed. (1) Capture: zero PNHU01 frames in either file - only a generic USB hub (VID 0x214b) and a Logitech Unifying receiver (VID 0x046d PID 0xc534) were captured; the hub's real CP210x (VID 0x10c4 PID 0xea60) never appeared. Root cause: picking one USBPcap interface by hand per run is exactly the trap capture.ps1 exists to avoid - the hub was on a controller other than the interface chosen. (2) License: Axis Studio (already installed, current PN3/Studio generation) requires a paid activation the owner doesn't have. Static analysis of its binaries for reusable protocol/CRC-8 structures came up empty - no v1-era markers (PNHU/CP210/Silicon Labs) anywhere, only current-generation model codes (N3T/U1H/U2H/U2P), so Axis Studio most likely dropped support for PNHU01 entirely - not worth analyzing further. Researched the activation system (403 on direct fetch to noitom.com/support.neuronmocap.com, pieced together from search snippets): current activation (account.noitom.com, Product ID) doesn't apply to this hardware generation; legacy activation used a physical Wibu dongle and Noitom appears to have stopped issuing new activations for it entirely.
